title: Flat tire or blowout: what to do now
metaDesc: Flat tire or blowout? Hold the wheel, ease off the gas, get to a safe spot. How to put on the spare, donut spare limits, sealant kits, and when to call.
first: If a tire blows while you're driving: hold the wheel firmly with both hands, keep going straight and ease off the gas. Don't slam the brakes.
Turn on your hazard lights. Brake gently once you've slowed down.
Pull fully off the road. A parking lot or side street is best. On a highway, take the next exit if you can, or use the right shoulder on flat, solid ground.
Engine off, parking brake on. Everyone waits away from the road.
Can't change it safely? Stay put and call roadside help.
dont: Don't change a tire on the traffic side, on a slope or on soft ground.
Never put any part of your body under the car while it's on the jack.
Don't drive on a tire with a bulge, a cut or cords showing.
Don't go over 50 mph on a small "donut" spare, and only drive it a short way.

steps.t: A parking lot or side street is safest. On a highway, take the next exit if you can. If not, use the right shoulder on a straight, flat, well-lit stretch.

Shift to Park (or reverse in a stick shift), turn the engine off, set the parking brake and leave the hazard lights on. Put wheel wedges, or big rocks, against the tire at the opposite corner from the flat. If you have cones or triangles, set them about 100 feet behind the car.
Find the spare, the jack and the lug wrench. Your owner's manual shows where they are and where the jack goes.
While the flat is still on the ground, loosen each lug nut a little by turning it to the left. Don't take them off yet. The car's weight keeps the wheel from spinning.
Put the jack under the metal frame at the spot your owner's manual shows, not under plastic. Raise the car until the flat tire is off the ground. Never put your body under the car.
Take off the lug nuts and pull the tire straight off, smoothly, so the car doesn't rock on the jack. Put the spare on and screw the nuts on by hand.
Snug each nut, going across to the opposite nut each time, not the one next to it. Lower the car, then tighten them all the way in the same star pattern.
Most small donut spares need about 60 PSI. The right number is on the spare or in your manual. Donuts are only for short trips: stay under 50 mph and get your own tire fixed or replaced soon.

steps.h: No spare? Using a sealant kit
steps.t: Many newer cars have a sealant and air pump kit instead of a spare. It can only fix a small puncture, like a nail hole in the tread (the part that touches the road). It can't fix a cut or hole in the sidewall. Follow the steps on the kit and in your owner's manual.

call: Call roadside help instead if you're missing a tool, you can't loosen the lug nuts, the spot isn't safe, the weather is bad, or you're not sure what to do.
Call 911 if you're stuck in a traffic lane or anyone is hurt.
